card: Reset request ID and JSON-RPC version fields at the beginning of request parsing rather than after validating object types. In a JSON-RPC batch, a malformed non-object element throws before resetting those fields on the reused request structure, causing the error reply to reuse the previous element's ID or suppress the error if the previous element was a notification. The author provides a new test in interface_rpc.py demonstrating the bug and verifying the fix.
changed_since_previous: None; the previous description was created without the diff, and the diff matches the previous description.
evidence: The author demonstrates that a batch like [{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2] generates two reply objects with id 'X' (one result and one error), and provides a new test case in test/functional/interface_rpc.py that fails on master and passes with this change (PR description)
problem: When processing a JSON-RPC batch, the server reuses a single JSONRPCRequest object across all items. If an element is not a JSON object, parse() throws an error before resetting the ID and version, causing the error response to reuse the previous element's ID or omit the error entirely if the previous element was a JSON-RPC 2.0 notification.

risk.why: A mistake in RPC request state handling could misformat or drop batch responses, confusing RPC clients.

summary: Reset the request ID and JSON-RPC version fields at the start of JSONRPCRequest::parse. This ensures malformed non-object elements in a batch request do not inherit the ID and version of the preceding element when generating error replies.
